summary.headline: Ddev Plastiks Q1 FY27 EBITDA crossed INR100 crore for the first time (INR101 cr, 10% margin), revenue up 29% YoY on export price gains.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 29% YoY and EBITDA rose 27% to about INR101 crore at a 10% margin, the first quarter above INR100 crore. PAT was about INR64 crore, up 22% YoY. Growth was driven mainly by export pricing (about INR300 crore export revenue, mostly MENA) rather than volume, with export volumes up only single digits and total volume up about 1% YoY. Capacity utilisation averaged about 66% as the new 48,000 t Bhiwadi XLPE plant, commissioned in April 2026, ramps up at roughly 20-25%. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 15% volume growth and a 13-14% revenue target, and said it expects to beat it.

financial_highlights.value: Up 29% YoY (absolute figure not stated in call)
INR101 crore approx; first time above INR100 crore

financial_highlights.change: Up in absolute terms; management cites about INR2.5-3 per ton of war/volatility premium

financial_highlights.value: About INR300-330 crore in Q1, partly carried over from Q4 shipments (~1,000 t)
Risen in Q1 due to working capital borrowing; management says easing from July

segments.name: Cables and wires (export)
segments.commentary: Primary growth driver in Q1; about INR300+ crore export revenue, mainly MENA, with pricing rather than volume the main gain. Management says export volume grew only single digits.

segments.name: XLPE compounds
segments.commentary: Installed XLPE capacity rose to 214,500 t after the 48,000 t Bhiwadi greenfield plant (commissioned April 2026); company holds more than one-third share of the XLPE segment. Bhiwadi expected to add about INR500 crore revenue at full utilisation.

segments.name: Engineering plastics
segments.commentary: Low volume but management cites 10-15% EBITDA margin; focus kept on lighting-industry niche (about 4 years of work).

segments.name: BESS (battery energy storage)
segments.commentary: New vertical; first phase about 1 GW / 1 GWh, supply model first, EBITDA margin 6-8% initially, capex plus working capital INR150-200 crore funded from internal accruals; timeline shifting by a couple of quarters, with mid-FY29 cited for 1 GW.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth target about 15%, with the target volume at 231,000 t and about 60,000 t per quarter needed for the remaining quarters.
FY27 revenue growth guidance about 13-14%, built on FY26 average realisation of about INR145/kg with no price increase assumed; management says it expects to beat guidance.
Long-term EBITDA margin target 10-12% (INR16-17/t), but Q1 EBITDA/t of about INR19.6 is not expected to be sustained every quarter.
Bhiwadi plant assumed at about 50% average utilisation in FY27, generating about INR200-250 crore of revenue; FY30 top-line ambition INR5,000 crore.
Resin prices expected to take 3-6 months to normalise after the Hormuz/war situation clears.
Committed capex for FY27 about INR150-175 crore (East MV cable capacity, HFFR expansion to 20,000 t, new Vapi site, BESS); about INR77 crore already spent in Q1.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity 316,400 t per annum as of June 2026; management cites 334,400 t by year-end and about 231,000 t planned FY27 tonnage.
Bhiwadi (Rajasthan) greenfield XLPE plant of 48,000 t commissioned April 2026, running at about 20-25% utilisation; expected to ramp over the next couple of months.
HFFR capacity to be expanded to 20,000 t by FY27 end; new Vapi site for product consolidation; PVC addition of about 25,000 t mentioned.

East India (Bengal) plant for medium-voltage cable compounds being set up; the BESS location is being shifted from West to East, delaying timelines by a couple of quarters, with the state incentive policy expected around end-August.
BESS phase 1 about 1 GW / 1 GWh, funded from internal accruals; BOO/BOOT not planned for now.
demand_pricing: Export pricing was the main Q1 driver: freight and raw material uncertainty let the company quote war-risk premiums, and management says export realisations rose about 30%.
Domestic demand softened in Q1 because of high polymer prices; management expects volume recovery once price volatility eases.
Management says the company's cable-customer segment grows about 12-13% a year, which is the basis for the 15% volume target, with the extra 2-3% expected to come from market share gains.
Share gain thesis: the Bhiwadi plant targets Rajasthan and Delhi customers; some western capacity moves to European exports.
Management expects EBITDA/t to stay elevated only for a few months; prices in July were marginally lower and August is 'okay', but orders are spot with 10-20 day visibility.
Cash conversion cycle widened in Q1 due to higher inventory and debtors; expected to return to 55-60 days.

qa_highlights.question: How much Q4 export revenue spilled into Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 1,000 t moved from late-March shipments; value rose due to freight, so about INR300+ crore export revenue was reported in Q1, partly from Q4 volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 EBITDA/t sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR19.6/t may not hold each quarter but could last a few months; the long-term target is INR16-17/t or 10-12% margin. The war-risk premium is about INR2.5-3/t.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS business model and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Starts as a supply model at 6-8% EBITDA margin, with EPC adding 2-5 points and system integrator another 2-3 points; long-term target 11-15%. BOO/BOOT not planned now.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 guidance (13-14% revenue) below capacity growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance uses FY26 average prices, assumes about 50% Bhiwadi utilisation and 15% volume growth; management says it expects to beat guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will finance costs and cash conversion cycle improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance costs rose from working-capital borrowing after the March raw material spike; they have eased since July. Cash conversion cycle expected to return to 55-60 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company gain market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management cites the Bhiwadi plant and importers being displaced by supply-chain disruption. Bhiwadi will serve existing customers, mainly in Rajasthan and Delhi.

risks_watch: Sustainability of Q1 EBITDA/t of about INR19.6: management says it may not hold each quarter and the long-term target is INR16-17/t; war-risk premium estimated at INR2.5-3/t and expected to shrink.

Volume growth gap: Q1 volume up only about 1% YoY against the 15% FY27 target, requiring about 60,000 t per quarter in Q2-Q4; recovery depends on Bhiwadi ramp (20-25% now, about 50% assumed) and domestic demand returning as polymer prices ease.
Export pricing exposure: prices eased marginally in July, export revenue for Q2 may be below the ~INR300-330 crore of Q1; order book is spot with 10-20 day visibility.
Resin and crude path: Hormuz situation and Iran-related announcements could keep prices volatile; management expects resin prices to take 3-6 months to normalise after the situation clears.

BESS execution: relocation from West to East delays timelines by a couple of quarters; 1 GW mid-FY29 timeline, state incentive policy expected around end-August; bids being retendered at low prices; margin 6-8% initially.

Working capital and finance cost: finance cost rose on working-capital borrowing and cash conversion cycle widened; management expects easing from July and CCC of 55-60 days, which needs to be verified in Q2.
key_quotes: So we expect an average utilization of 50-plus percent from that.
It is very difficult to predict on this line.
So, if you ask in terms of numbers, technically, it may be around 1,000-odd tons, which has been moved, but the value has changed later on because of increase in freight and all.
As far as the approval process is concerned from the new site, it is no special or new approval is required.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and the full-year beat, but cautious on forward pricing and volumes: management repeatedly declined to guide beyond August, calling the outlook highly uncertain. Confidence is most evident on capacity, approvals and the 15% volume target, while answers on BESS timing and the Q2 export number were hedged and included corrections.
